question: Which aggregation router has the most cell sites down right now?
How many subscribers and which enterprise accounts are affected by the sites that are down right now?
Which cells have the biggest increase in dropped-call rate over the last 3 weeks?
What is our average MTTR by trouble-ticket category over the last 12 months?
What share of outages had an early warning that was ignored, by category?
What priority is a fiber cut that takes down a hospital's cell sites, and who must be notified by when under the NOC runbooks?

content:
Halcyon Wireless — fictional Mountain-West regional carrier (synthetic data): 500 cell sites (3 sectors A/B/C each; cell_id = <site_id>-<sector>) in 5 markets (Denver Metro, Boulder, Fort Collins, Colorado Springs, Pueblo). Each site backhauls through ONE aggregation router (cell_sites.agg_router_id); aggregation routers connect to core routers CORE-DEN-01 (primary fiber, xe-0/1/0) and CORE-DEN-02 (secondary fiber, xe-0/1/1) — see transport_links.
All timestamps are Mountain local time. 'Now', 'right now', 'currently', 'today' = the latest data, NOT current_timestamp(): use gold_site_status (as_of_ts = latest reported hour) for sites down / current state, max(raised_ts) of silver_alarms for 'last 24 hours' of alarms, and max(day) of gold_cell_kpi_daily for KPI windows.
A site is DOWN when gold_site_status.is_down = true (availability < 50% in the latest hour). Dropped-call rate = 100 * dropped_calls / voice_calls (use gold_cell_kpi_daily.drop_call_rate_pct per cell-day). Targets: dropped-call rate < 0.8%, RRC setup success > 99%, VSWR < 1.5 (vendor alarm at 2.0).
silver_alarms: one row per alarm, is_active = not cleared; severity critical > major > minor > warning. An alarm storm = many sites alarming under the same agg_router_id within minutes.
noc_incidents = the correlated open incident queue (alarm_storm / power_alarm / backhaul_alarm / site_outage / kpi_anomaly). cell_health_daily = KPI anomaly model scores (anomaly_score 0-100, is_anomaly >= 70).
Customer impact: subscribers_served per site (cell_sites / gold_site_status), enterprise_site_coverage (account, sla_tier, restore_sla_hours) joined on site_id.
trouble_tickets = 12 months of closed tickets (mttr_hours = restore time); trouble_ticket_insights.precursor (AI-classified from resolution notes) = early warning ignored | sudden failure | planned or external cause.
Round percentages to 1 decimal and give subscriber counts as integers.

ROUTING: numbers, counts, amounts, rates, trends -> query the TABLES (SQL); never answer numbers from a document. Policy, procedure, guideline, contract and 'what does the document say' questions -> search the attached documents and cite the document name + section.

question: How many subscribers and which enterprise accounts are affected by the sites that are down right now?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT s.site_id) AS sites_down, sum(s.subscribers_served) AS subscribers, (SELECT collect_set(concat(e.account_name, ' (', e.sla_tier, ', ', e.restore_sla_hours, 'h SLA)')) FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.enterprise_site_coverage e JOIN telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.gold_site_status d ON d.site_id = e.site_id WHERE d.is_down) AS enterprise_accounts_affected, collect_set(s.critical_facility) AS critical_facilities FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.gold_site_status s WHERE s.is_down

question: What share of outages had an early warning that was ignored, by category?
sql: SELECT category, count(*) AS tickets, count_if(precursor = 'early warning ignored') AS early_warning_ignored, round(100 * count_if(precursor = 'early warning ignored') / count(*), 1) AS pct_early_warning_ignored, round(avg(IF(precursor = 'early warning ignored', mttr_hours, NULL)), 1) AS mttr_when_warned_hours FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.trouble_ticket_insights GROUP BY category ORDER BY pct_early_warning_ignored DESC

question: Which cells have the biggest increase in dropped-call rate over the last 3 weeks?
sql: WITH d AS (SELECT max(day) m FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.gold_cell_kpi_daily) SELECT k.cell_id, round(avg(IF(k.day <= d.m - 18, k.drop_call_rate_pct, NULL)), 2) AS drop_rate_3_weeks_ago_pct, round(avg(IF(k.day >= d.m - 2, k.drop_call_rate_pct, NULL)), 2) AS drop_rate_last_3_days_pct, round(avg(IF(k.day >= d.m - 2, k.drop_call_rate_pct, NULL)) - avg(IF(k.day <= d.m - 18, k.drop_call_rate_pct, NULL)), 2) AS increase_pts, round(max(IF(k.day >= d.m - 2, k.max_vswr, NULL)), 2) AS vswr_now FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.gold_cell_kpi_daily k, d WHERE k.day >= d.m - 20 GROUP BY k.cell_id ORDER BY increase_pts DESC LIMIT 10

question: What is our average MTTR by trouble-ticket category over the last 12 months?
sql: SELECT category, count(*) AS tickets, round(avg(mttr_hours), 1) AS avg_mttr_hours, round(percentile_approx(mttr_hours, 0.5), 1) AS median_mttr_hours, sum(subscribers_affected) AS subscribers_affected FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.trouble_tickets GROUP BY category ORDER BY avg_mttr_hours DESC

question: How many alarms did we receive in the last 24 hours by severity?
sql: SELECT severity, count(*) AS alarms, count_if(is_active) AS still_active, count(DISTINCT coalesce(site_id, node_id)) AS nodes FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.silver_alarms WHERE raised_ts > (SELECT max(raised_ts) FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.silver_alarms) - INTERVAL 24 HOURS GROUP BY severity ORDER BY CASE severity WHEN 'critical' THEN 1 WHEN 'major' THEN 2 WHEN 'minor' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END

question: Which aggregation router has the most cell sites down right now?
sql: SELECT agg_router_id, count_if(is_down) AS sites_down, count(*) AS sites_homed, sum(IF(is_down, subscribers_served, 0)) AS subscribers_on_down_sites, max(as_of_ts) AS as_of FROM telecommunications.network_ops_copilot.gold_site_status GROUP BY agg_router_id ORDER BY sites_down DESC LIMIT 5
